# Background

We conducted this experiment to investigate the genetic components of BX-feedbacks. We have previously shown than BX-feedbacks are genetically imprinted in Arabidopsis accessions. We used a GWAS approach to identify candidate genes that are associated with BX-feedbacks. We grew 410 Arabidopsis accessions under controlled conditions on BXplus and BXminus soils and measured the growth feedback. We used LIMIX and the `gwaR` package to perform the GWAS analysis (@lippert2014) and extract candidate genes (@hüther2020).

# Materials and methods

We grew 410 Arabidopsis accessions under controlled conditions. We used a randomized block design with 3 replicates per accession. We grew the plants in a growth chamber with automated phenotyping and extracted phenotypes using ARADEEPOPSIS (@hüther2020). We measured the growth feedback as the plant_region_area between plants grown on BXplus and BXminus soils. We used the `gwaR` package to perform the GWAS analysis.

-   **Purpose**: To identify candidate genes that are associated with BX-feedbacks.

# Data Preparation

## Filter the SNP Table

We filter the SNP table and phenotype table to include only the data for the first 20 days after germination (DAG 0 to DAG 20). A lot of accessions started to flower at this point which affected the phenotyping.

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#| label: table-SNP-table
#| paged-print: false
#| tbl-cap: Table containing the SNP output data
# Filter SNPs for phenotypes from DAG 0 to DAG 20
tot_plant_specific_snps_DAG20 <- filter(tot_plant_specific_snps, dag < 22)
tot_plant_specific_snps_DAG20 <- 
  tot_plant_specific_snps_DAG20[order(tot_plant_specific_snps_DAG20$log10_p, 
                                      decreasing = TRUE),]

# Modify the SNP table to correctly show the days after germination, starting from DAG=0 by adding +1 to each value in the "dag" column

tot_plant_specific_snps_DAG20 <- tot_plant_specific_snps_DAG20 %>%
  mutate(dag = dag - 1)

kable(tot_plant_specific_snps_DAG20[1:5, ], caption = "SNP table for DAG<20.")

# Purpose: Filters the SNP data to include only data from days after germination (DAG) 0 to 20.
```

## Manhattan plot

```{r}
#| label: fig-Manhattan-plot
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: Manhattan plot showing the top 500 SNPs identified in the GWAS.
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 10
#| paged-print: false
# Create the Manhattan plot
manhattan_plot <- tot_plant_specific_snps_DAG20 %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = pos, y = log10_p, label = pos)) +
  
  # Add alternating shading for every second facet
  geom_rect(
    data = tot_plant_specific_snps_DAG20 %>% 
      distinct(chrom) %>% 
      mutate(shade = row_number() %% 2 == 0), # Create a flag for shading
    aes(
      xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
      fill = shade
    ), 
    inherit.aes = FALSE, alpha = 0.1
  ) +
  
  # Add points
  geom_point(aes(fill = Significant, color = Significant), 
             size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
  
  # Styling and themes
  theme(
    # Remove panel grid lines and background
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    # Add axis line
    axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
    # Adjust legend position
    legend.position = c(0.09, 0.80),
    # Remove x-axis ticks and labels
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    # Set all text to size 7pt
    axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 7),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 7)
  ) +
  
  expand_limits(y = c(10, 5)) +
  
  facet_grid(~chrom, scales = "free_x", switch = "x") +
  
  scale_color_manual(values = c("red4", "slategray4", "slategray4")) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey", "grey", "grey","grey","grey"), 
                    guide = "none") + # Alternate shading colors
  
  ggtitle("Manhattan plot")

# Display the plot
print(manhattan_plot)


# Purpose: Displays the Manhattan plot.

# Save the plot
ggsave("Manhattan_plot.pdf", plot = manhattan_plot, height = 7.0, width = 16.3, units = "cm", path = "Output/Figures")
# Purpose: Saves the Manhattan plot as a PDF file.
```

-   **Purpose**: The Manhattan plot visualizes the significance of SNPs across chromosomes, highlighting significant SNPs.

## Find Closest Genes to Top SNPs

We bioinformatically isolate the genes located closest to the top 10 SNPs identified in the GWAs analysis using the `get_nearest_genes` function.

```{r}
#| label: table-gene-table
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false
#| tbl-cap: Table containing the SNPs and the genes located closest to each of the top SNPs
nearest_genes <- tot_plant_specific_snps_DAG20 %>% 
  get_nearest_genes(n_hit = 100)
# Purpose: Identifies the 20 closest genes to the top SNPs using the `get_nearest_genes` function.

kable(nearest_genes[1:10, 1:7], caption = "Table with genes located closest to the top SNPs.")
# Purpose: Displays the nearest genes to the top SNPs.
```

```{r}
#| label: Manhattat plot
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false
# Compute chromosome sizes
don <- tot_plant_specific_snps_DAG20 %>% 
  group_by(chrom) %>% 
  summarise(chr_len = max(pos)) %>% 
  
  # Calculate cumulative position for each chromosome
  mutate(tot = cumsum(chr_len) - chr_len) %>%
  select(-chr_len) %>%
  
  # Merge back to original dataset
  left_join(tot_plant_specific_snps_DAG20, ., by = c("chrom" = "chrom")) %>%
  
  # Compute cumulative SNP position
  arrange(chrom, pos) %>%
  mutate(BPcum = pos + tot)

# Compute chromosome midpoints for x-axis labels
axisdf <- don %>%
  group_by(chrom) %>%
  summarise(center = (max(BPcum) + min(BPcum)) / 2)

# Plot

plot <- ggplot(don, aes(x = BPcum, y = log10_p)) +
  geom_point(
    aes(color = ifelse(Significant == "Bonferroni", "red4", as.factor(chrom))),
    alpha = 0.8, size = 1
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "red4" = "red4",
      setNames(rep(c( "#A0A0A0", "#00798c"), length(unique(don$chrom))), unique(don$chrom))
    )
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = -log10(0.05 / nrow(don)),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "gray30",
    size = 0.4
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "Chromosome",
    labels = axisdf$chrom,
    breaks = axisdf$center,
    expand = c(0.01, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = expression(-log[10](italic(p))),
    limits = c(4.8, 10),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  ggtitle("Manhattan Plot") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),  # Removes ALL major gridlines
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),  # Removes ALL minor gridlines
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.5),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 7),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 7, hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

print(plot)
ggsave("Manhattan_plot.pdf", plot = plot, height = 7, width = 16.3, units = "cm", path = "Output/Figures")
```

# Geographic distribution of Accessions

We first create a world map that will be used to plot the geographic distribution of Arabidopsis accessions based on their SNP response to BX-feedbacks.

```{r}
#| label: Prep Geo plot
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
#| paged-print: false
# Load necessary libraries
library(maps)
# Purpose: Loads the `maps` package for map plotting.

# Load world map data
world_map <- map_data("world")
# Purpose: Loads data for the world map.

# Load ACC coordinates data
ACC_coordinates <- read_excel("Input/Dataset3.xlsx", 
                              sheet = "Accessions_coordinates")
# Purpose: Loads ACC coordinates data from a CSV file.

# Subset the world map data for the region of interest
World_map_small <- subset(world_map, long > -130 & long < 90)
World_map_small <- subset(World_map_small, lat > -0 & lat < 90)
# Purpose: Filters the world map data to focus on a specific region.

# Create a base plot with ggplot2
p <- ggplot() + coord_fixed() +
  xlab("Longitude") + ylab("Latitude")
# Purpose: Initializes a ggplot2 object for mapping with fixed coordinates.

# Add map to base plot
base_world_messy <- p + geom_polygon(data = World_map_small, aes(x = long, 
                                                                 y = lat, 
                                                                 group = group), 
                                     colour = "grey90", fill = "grey90")
# Purpose: Adds the filtered map data to the base plot as polygons.

# Display the messy base world map
#print(base_world_messy)
# Purpose: Displays the unrefined world map.

# Strip the map down to make it clean and beautiful
cleanup <- theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), 
                 panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
                 panel.background = element_rect(fill = 'white', 
                                                 colour = 'white'), 
                 axis.line = element_line(colour = "grey50"))
# Purpose: Cleans up the map by removing unnecessary elements and applying a minimalist theme.

base_world <- base_world_messy + cleanup
# Purpose: Applies the cleaned-up theme to the world map.

# Display the clean base world map
#print(base_world)
# Purpose: Displays the refined world map.
```

# Phenotypic effect of SNPMMF1

We investigate the phenotypic effect of SNPMMF1 on the BX-feedback response of Arabidopsis accessions. We use the `phenotype_by_snp` function to extract the plant region area and days after germination (DAG) data for SNPMMF1.

```{r}
#| label: Isolate top SNP effect
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false
# Extract plant area
temp1 <- tot_plant_specific_snps %>%
  {gwaR::phenotype_by_snp(plant_region_areas %>% mutate(ACC_ID = genotype_id),
                          "plant_region_area",
                          gwas_table = .,
                          specific = "bx",
                          SNPrank = 7,
                          plot = FALSE,
                          SNPmatrix = "Input/SNPmatrix_full.fst", # Ensure this path is correct
                          nobees = TRUE)}


# Extract dag (days after germination)

temp2 <- tot_plant_specific_snps %>%
  {gwaR::phenotype_by_snp(plant_region_areas %>% mutate(ACC_ID = genotype_id),
                          "dag",
                          gwas_table = .,
                          specific = "bx",
                          SNPrank = 7,
                          plot = FALSE,
                          SNPmatrix = "Input/SNPmatrix_full.fst", # Ensure this path is correct
                          nobees = TRUE)}

# Combine extracted data into one data frame

plant_region_areas_SNP <- data.frame(ACC_ID = temp1$ACC_ID,
                          bx = temp1$bx,
                          plant_region_area = temp1$phenotype_value,
                          dag = as.integer(temp2$phenotype_value),
                          SNP = temp1$SNP) # Convert dag to integers

rm(temp1, temp2)

kable(plant_region_areas_SNP[1:5, ], caption = "Table with plant region area by SNP.")
```

## Subset the Data to Phenotypes at Day 15

We do this to focus on the phenotypic effects of SNPMM1 on growth. We choose DAG15, since this is the latest time when the genetic association of SNPMMF1 was still visible.

```{r}
#| label: Subset DAG 15
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

# Subset to plants with exactly 15 days old
plant_region_areas_DAG15 <- 
  plant_region_areas_SNP[plant_region_areas_SNP$dag == 15, -6]
# Purpose: Filters the data to include only plants that are exactly 15 days old.

# Compute mean per ACC
plant_region_areas_DAG15 <- plant_region_areas_DAG15 %>%
  group_by(bx, ACC_ID) %>%
  mutate(mean_ACC = mean(plant_region_area, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()
# Purpose: Calculates the mean plant region area for each ACC_ID within each bx group.

# Remove unnecessary columns and keep unique entries
plant_region_areas_DAG15 <- plant_region_areas_DAG15 %>%
  select(-plant_region_area, -dag) %>%
  distinct()
# Purpose: Removes unnecessary columns and retains only unique rows in the data frame.

# Spread the data by bx treatment
plant_region_areas_DAG15 <- plant_region_areas_DAG15 %>%
  spread(key = bx, value = mean_ACC)
# Purpose: Reshapes the data so that bx treatments are in separate columns.

# Calculate the difference between treatments (bx+ - bx-)
plant_region_areas_DAG15 <- plant_region_areas_DAG15 %>%
  mutate(area_diff = `+` - `-`,
         fold_change = `+` / `-`,
         excessive = case_when(
           fold_change >= 1.5 ~ "plus",
           fold_change <= -1.5 ~ "minus",
           fold_change < 1.5 ~ "neutral"
         )) %>%
  arrange(desc(area_diff))
# Purpose: Calculates the difference in plant region area between bx+ and bx- treatments, and classifies the results.

# Add preference column based on growth feedback
plant_region_areas_DAG15 <- plant_region_areas_DAG15 %>%
  mutate(preference = case_when(
    area_diff >= 0 ~ "plus",
    TRUE ~ "minus"
  )) %>%
  arrange(desc(area_diff)) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number())
# Purpose: Assigns a preference (plus or minus) based on growth feedback and ranks the accessions by area difference.

# Rank by area_diff
plant_region_areas_DAG15 <- plant_region_areas_DAG15 %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number(dplyr::desc(area_diff)))
# Purpose: Ranks the accessions based on the area difference in descending order.

# Save the result to a CSV file
write.csv(plant_region_areas_DAG15, row.names = TRUE, file = "Output/Plant_region_areas_DAG15.csv")
# Purpose: Saves the final data frame to a CSV file.

# Display the final dataframe
kable(plant_region_areas_DAG15[1:5, ], caption = "Table with accession growth feedback and feedback response")
# Purpose: Displays the first few rows of the final data frame.

```

-   **Purpose**: The data is filtered to include only plants that are exactly 15 days old. The mean plant region area for each ACC_ID within each bx group is calculated. The data is reshaped so that bx treatments are in separate columns. The difference in plant region area between bx+ and bx- treatments is calculated, and the results are classified. The accessions are ranked based on the area difference, and the final data frame is saved to a CSV file.

# **5. Effect of SNPs linked to SNPMMF1**

Here we identify SNPs that are linked to SNPMMF1 using the `linkage_phenotypes` function and calculate the mean plant region area at each SNP for acessions with and without the SNP.

## Identify linked SNPs

```{r}
#| label: SNP linkage
#| eval: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
#| paged-print: false

plant_region_areas_dag15 <- plant_region_areas %>% filter(dag == 15)
# Purpose: Filters the plant region areas data to include only observations at 15 days after germination.

linkage_Pheno_table <- linkage_phenotypes(plant_region_areas_dag15 %>% 
                                            mutate(ACC_ID = genotype_id), 
                   phenotype = "plant_region_area", 
                   chrom = 3,
                   pos = 16203882,
                  nuc_range = 50000,
                  ld_stats = "LLR",
                  SNPmatrix = "Input/SNPmatrix_full.fst",
                  specific = c("bx", "dag"),
                  impacts = c("MODERATE", "HIGH"))
kable(linkage_Pheno_table[1:5, ], caption = "Table with genomic region surrounding SNPMMF1.")
```

-   **Purpose**: The average plant region area at each SNP is calculated using the `linkage_phenotypes` function.

### Calculate the Mean Plant Region Area at Each SNP for each accession

```{r}
#| label: Effect of linked SNPs
#| eval: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
#| paged-print: false

# Get mean per ACC
linkage_Pheno_table_ACC <- linkage_Pheno_table
linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$mean_ACC <- NA  # Initialize an empty vector
# Loop through unique combinations of bx, pos, SNP, and ACC_ID
for (bx in unique(linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$bx)) {
  for (pos in unique(linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$pos)) {
    for (SNP in unique(linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$SNP)) {
      for (ACC_ID in unique(linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$ACC_ID)) {
        # Compute the mean for the current combination of bx, pos, SNP, and ACC_ID
        mean_ACC <- mean(linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$phenotype_value[
                            linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$bx == bx &
                            linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$pos == pos &
                            linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$SNP == SNP &
                            linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$ACC_ID == ACC_ID], 
                         na.rm = TRUE)  # use na.rm=TRUE to handle missing values
        
        # Store the computed mean in the mean_ACC column
        linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$mean_ACC[
          linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$bx == bx &
          linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$pos == pos &
          linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$SNP == SNP &
          linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$ACC_ID == ACC_ID
        ] <- mean_ACC
      }
    }
  }
}
                                                            
# Remove replicates from the data frame
linkage_Pheno_table_ACC <- linkage_Pheno_table_ACC[,c(-4, -5)] # Remove specific columns (area and dag)
linkage_Pheno_table_ACC <- distinct(linkage_Pheno_table_ACC) # Keep only unique entries

# Spread by bx treatment
linkage_Pheno_table_ACC <- spread(linkage_Pheno_table_ACC, 
                                  key = "bx", value = "mean_ACC")
# Purpose: Reshapes the data so that bx treatments are in separate columns.

# Calculate the difference between treatments (bx+ - bx-)
linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$area_diff <- linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$`+` - linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$`-`
linkage_Pheno_table_ACC <- linkage_Pheno_table_ACC[order(linkage_Pheno_table_ACC$pos, decreasing = F),]
```

## Calculate the Mean Plant Region Area at Each SNP

```{r}
#| label: Mean area per SNP
#| eval: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
#| paged-print: false

# Get mean per ACC
linkage_Pheno_table$mean_ACC <- NA # Initialize an empty vector

for (bx in unique(linkage_Pheno_table$bx)) {
  for (pos in unique(linkage_Pheno_table$pos)) {
    for (SNP in unique(linkage_Pheno_table$SNP)) {
      # Compute mean
      mean_ACC <- mean(linkage_Pheno_table$phenotype_value[linkage_Pheno_table$bx==bx &
                                                            linkage_Pheno_table$pos==pos &
                                                            linkage_Pheno_table$SNP==SNP])
      # Store mean
      linkage_Pheno_table$mean_ACC[linkage_Pheno_table$bx==bx &
                                  linkage_Pheno_table$pos==pos &
                                  linkage_Pheno_table$SNP==SNP] <- mean_ACC
    }
  }
}
# Purpose: Computes the mean plant region area for each combination of bx, pos, and SNP, and stores the results.

# Remove replicates from the data frame
linkage_Pheno_table <- linkage_Pheno_table[,c(-1,-4, -5)] # Remove specific columns (area and dag)
linkage_Pheno_table <- distinct(linkage_Pheno_table) # Keep only unique entries
# Purpose: Removes unnecessary columns and keeps only unique rows in the data frame.

# Spread by bx treatment
linkage_Pheno_table <- spread(linkage_Pheno_table, key = "bx", value = "mean_ACC")
# Purpose: Reshapes the data so that bx treatments are in separate columns.

# Calculate the difference between treatments (bx+ - bx-)
linkage_Pheno_table$area_diff <- linkage_Pheno_table$`+` - linkage_Pheno_table$`-`
linkage_Pheno_table <- linkage_Pheno_table[order(linkage_Pheno_table$pos, decreasing = F),] # Sort by difference
# Purpose: Calculates the difference in plant region area between bx+ and bx- treatments and sorts the data by position.
kable(linkage_Pheno_table[1:5, 1:7], caption = "Table with SNPs linked to SNPMMF1 and the effects on feedbacks.")

```

-   **Purpose**: The mean plant region area at each SNP is calculated, and the data is reshaped to show bx treatments in separate columns. The difference in plant region area between bx+ and bx- treatments is calculated, and the data is sorted by position.

# Genomic exploration

### Load Arabidopsis Genome Data

We load the Arabidopsis genome data from the Ensembl Plants database using the `biomaRt` package.

```{r}
#| label: Genomic data
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false
# Load necessary libraries
library(biomaRt)
library(stringr)
library(plyranges)
# Purpose: Loads the necessary libraries for working with genomic data.

araGenome <- biomaRt::getBM(c("ensembl_gene_id",
                              "chromosome_name",
                              "start_position",
                              "end_position",
                              "strand",
                              "description",
                              "transcript_biotype"),
                            mart = biomaRt::useMart(biomart = "plants_mart", 
                                                    dataset = "athaliana_eg_gene", 
                                                    host = 'plants.ensembl.org'))
# Purpose: Retrieves genomic data for Arabidopsis thaliana from the Ensembl Plants database using `biomaRt`.
```

### Format Arabidopsis Genome Data as GRanges

We format the Arabidopsis genome data as a GRanges object, which is suitable for genomic range operations. We also prepare gene labels for plotting by filtering and mutating the genomic data. Finally, we filter the Arabidopsis genome data to include only the specific region surrounding SNPMMMF1 on chromosome 3.

```{r}
#| label: Format Genomic data
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

#| label: tab-Gen-reg-SNPMMF1
#| fig-cap: "The table of all the genes in the region of SNPMMF1."

# Format araGenome as a GRanges object
araGenes <- araGenome %>%
  dplyr::rename(GeneId=ensembl_gene_id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(strand=dplyr::case_when(strand == 1 ~ "+",
                                        strand == -1 ~ "-"),
                start = start_position,
                end = end_position) %>%
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(chromosome_name,"[1-9]")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(seqnames=paste0("Chr",chromosome_name)) %>%
  plyranges::as_granges()
# Purpose: Formats the Arabidopsis genome data as a GRanges object, which is suitable for genomic range operations.

gene_labels <- araGenome %>%
      dplyr::filter(chromosome_name == chromosome_name,
                    start_position %in% c(start_position:end_position),
                    end_position %in% c(start_position:end_position)) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(gene = ensembl_gene_id,
                    molecule = 0,
                    start = start_position,
                    end = end_position,
                    direction = strand,
                    strand = dplyr::case_when(strand == -1 ~ "reverse", 
                                              TRUE ~ "forward"),
                    layer_var = "ORF")
# Purpose: Prepares gene labels for plotting by filtering and mutating the genomic data.

araGenome_filt <- araGenome %>% filter(chromosome_name == "3", 
                                       start_position >= 16170000, 
                                       end_position <= 16230000)
# Purpose: Filters the Arabidopsis genome data to include only a specific region on chromosome 3.
kable(araGenome_filt[1:5, 1:5], caption = "Table with genomic region surrounding SNPMMF1.")

```

            panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank())+

           fill = "lightgrey", alpha = 0.4) +
  # Horizontal shading
  #annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = 4.5, ymax = Inf, 
           #fill = "lightgrey", alpha = 0.4) +
  # Line denoting SNP of interest
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = 16203882), color = "darkred", 
             size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
  
  # SNPs
  annotate("rect", xmin = 16195848, xmax = 16201225, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
           fill = "grey", alpha = 0.02) +
  geom_point(aes(x = pos, y = log10_p, color = Significant), 
             size = 2.0, alpha = 0.8) +
  
  # Color scale for `Significant`
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("red4", "slategray4"), name = "Significant") +
  
  # Gene annotations
  gggenes::geom_gene_arrow(arrowhead_width = grid::unit(4, "mm"),
                           arrowhead_height = grid::unit(7, "mm"),
                           arrow_body_height = grid::unit(5, "mm"),
                           aes(xmin = start_position, xmax = end_position, 
                               y = 4, forward = strand == "1"), 
                           fill = "lightblue2", data = araGenome_filt) +
  gggenes::geom_gene_label(aes(xmin = start_position, xmax = end_position, y = 4, 
                               label = ensembl_gene_id), min.size = 6, 
                           data = araGenome_filt) +
  
  # Minimal theme
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(0, "lines"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank()
  ) +
  
  expand_limits(y = c(0.9, 9), x = c(16198882, 16208882))  # Adjusted limits to move axis downward

# Add the secondary plot
combined_plot <- plot_SNPs +
  new_scale_color() +  # Use a new color scale for the secondary plot
  geom_point(data = SNPMMF1_linkage, 
             aes(x = pos, y = effect_position,  # Use manual positions for y
                 color = value, shape = effect_impact), 
             size = 2.0, alpha = 0.8) +
  
  # Secondary y-axis for `effect_impact`
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "log10_p",  # Left axis
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ .,  # No transformation needed
      name = "Linkage Distance",
      breaks = c(0.9, 1.7, 2.5, 3.3),  # Use manual positions
      labels = c("MODIFIER", "LOW", "MODERATE", "HIGH")  # Explicit order
    )
  ) +
 
  geom_label(aes(label = "SNPMMF1", x = 16203882, y = 9), size = 3.5, 
             fill = "white", color = "grey40")+
  # Color gradient for `value`
  scale_color_gradient(low = "blue2", high = "yellow", name = "Effect Value") +
  
  # Adjust text for secondary axis
  theme(
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(color = "black")
  )

# Print the combined plot
combined_plot

#| label: Genomic region urrounding top SNP
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false
tot_plant_specific_snps_DAG20_chrm3_filt <- tot_plant_specific_snps_DAG20 %>% 
          filter(chrom == 3) %>% 
          filter(pos > 16170000 & pos < 16230000)



# Define the primary plot
plot_SNPs <- ggplot(data = tot_plant_specific_snps_DAG20_chrm3_filt) +
    
    # Horizontal shading
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = 3.5, ymax = 4.5, 
             fill = "lightgrey", alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_vline(aes(xintercept = 16203882), color = "darkred", size = 0.6, 
               alpha = 0.6) +
    
    # SNPs
    annotate("rect", xmin = 16195848, xmax = 16201225, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
             fill = "grey", alpha = 0.02) +
    geom_point(aes(x = pos, y = log10_p, color = Significant), size = 2.0, 
               alpha = 0.8) +
    
    # Color scale for `Significant`
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("red4", "slategray4"), name = "Significant") +
    
    # Gene annotations with specific gene coloring and alpha
    gggenes::geom_gene_arrow(
        arrowhead_width = grid::unit(3, "mm"),
        arrowhead_height = grid::unit(6, "mm"),
        arrow_body_height = grid::unit(4, "mm"),
        aes(
            xmin = start_position, xmax = end_position, y = 4,
            forward = strand == "1",
            fill = ifelse(ensembl_gene_id %in% c("AT3G44630", "AT3G44670"), 
                          "TNLs", "non-TNLs"),
            alpha = ifelse(ensembl_gene_id %in% c("AT3G44630", "AT3G44670"), 
                           0.5, 0.7) # Different alpha levels
        ), 
        data = araGenome_filt
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
        values = c("TNLs" = "orange", "non-TNLs" = "lightblue2"),
        name = "Genes"
    ) +
    scale_alpha_continuous(
        range = c(0.8, 0.6), # Ensure alpha is within valid range
        guide = "none"       # Suppress alpha legend
    ) +
    
    # Gene labels
    gggenes::geom_gene_label(
        aes(xmin = start_position, xmax = end_position, y = 4, 
            label = ensembl_gene_id), 
        min.size = 4, 
        data = araGenome_filt
    ) +
    
    # Minimal theme
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing.y = unit(0, "lines"),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA),
        panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank()
    ) +
    
    expand_limits(y = c(3.5, 9), x = c(16198882, 16208882)) +
    geom_label(aes(label = "SNPMMF1", x = 16203882, y = 8.8), size = 2.5, 
               fill = "white", color = "grey40") +
    
    # Adjust text for secondary axis
    theme(
        axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "black"),
        axis.text.y.right = element_text(color = "black")
    )

# Print the combined plot
plot_SNPs
ggsave("SNPs_MMF1_region.pdf", height = 6, width = 10, units = "cm", dpi = 600, path = "Output/Figures")

#| label: Export data

# Load the package
library(openxlsx)

# Create a new workbook
Dataset3 <- createWorkbook()

# Add worksheets and data
addWorksheet(Dataset3, "SNP_table_dag20")
writeData(Dataset3, "SNP_table_dag20", tot_plant_specific_snps_DAG20)

addWorksheet(Dataset3, "SNP_gene_table")
writeData(Dataset3, "SNP_gene_table", nearest_genes)

addWorksheet(Dataset3, "Accessions_SNPMMF1_DAG15")
writeData(Dataset3, "Accessions_SNPMMF1_DAG15", plant_region_areas_DAG15)

# Subset the required columns (1, 2, 7, 8, 9, and 10)
subset_data <- ACC_coordinates[, c(1, 7, 8, 9, 10)]
addWorksheet(Dataset3, "Accessions_coordinates")
writeData(Dataset3, "Accessions_coordinates", subset_data)

# Save the workbook to an Excel file
saveWorkbook(Dataset3, file = "Output/Tables/Dataset3.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
